props.closer: Master the basics — everything else is built on them.

captions: Welcome to the complete course on equities, futures, options,
and commodities.
This is a long, structured masterclass.
We start from the very basics — what these instruments are —
and build up, step by step,
to the strategies professional investors and traders actually use.
We will cover how to pick a sector, how to research a stock,
where to find trustworthy research,
futures and options explained simply, commodities,
and every major strategy for each.
One promise up front: this is education, not tips.
We will never tell you what to buy.
We will teach you how to think, so you can decide for yourself.
Here is the roadmap.
Six big blocks.
First — which sector to select,
using a top-down method the professionals use.
Second — how to research a stock, both the fundamentals,
the business and its numbers, and the technicals,
the price chart.
Third —
where to find genuine research: the trustworthy YouTube channels,
data tools, and market voices,
and how to tell a real source from a tip-seller.
Fourth — futures and options, explained from zero,
with every major strategy.
Fifth — commodities: gold, silver, and crude oil on the MCX.
And running through all of it — sixth — risk management,
the discipline that decides who survives.
Let's begin with the big picture.
There are four arenas we will master.
The first is equities.
This is ownership.
When you buy a share, you own a small slice of a real business,
and you grow as it grows.
This is where wealth is built.
The second is futures.
A future is a contract to buy or sell something later,
at a price fixed today.
It is leveraged and it expires.
It is a derivative —
its value derives from an underlying asset.
The third is options.
An option gives you the right, but not the obligation,
to buy or sell at a set price,
for a small fee called a premium.
Also a derivative.
The fourth is commodities — gold, silver, crude oil —
traded on the MCX, mostly through futures.
Equities are for investing.
Futures and options are powerful but risky tools.
Commodities are a world of their own.
We will do them all.
Before we go deeper, the plumbing —
how the Indian market actually works.
Buyers and sellers meet on two exchanges: the National Stock Exchange,
founded 1992, and the Bombay Stock Exchange, Asia's oldest,
from 1875.
Watching over everyone is the regulator, SEBI —
the Securities and Exchange Board of India.
Think of it as the umpire whose job is to protect you.
Your shares are held digitally, in a demat account,
with one of two depositories, NSDL or CDSL.
To trade you need a demat plus a trading account —
most brokers open both together.
When you buy,
the shares reach your account the next working day —
that's T plus one settlement.
And the market is open from nine-fifteen in the morning to three-thirty in the afternoon,
Monday to Friday.
That's the stage.
Now the play.
Let's lock in chapter one.
There are four arenas: equities, futures, options,
and commodities.
Equities are ownership; futures and options are derivatives; commodities trade on the MCX.
The NSE and BSE are the exchanges, SEBI is the regulator,
your shares sit in a demat account,
and settlement is T plus one.
And the spirit of this course: we learn to think for ourselves —
we never blindly follow tips.
Next, the first real skill: how to choose a sector.
